statusText: Calm, wait-and-see conditions persist into the European late morning ahead of today's 12:30 UTC Retail Sales / 14:00 UTC preliminary UMich data cluster. Chip stocks are broadly firmer in premarket trading (Nvidia, TSMC, Broadcom, SK Hynix, Micron, AMD all higher) following Thursday's soft-PPI record close (S&P 500 +0.65% to 7,798.99; Nasdaq Composite +0.81% to 26,803.03). VIX holds flat near 14.4-14.8 and the 10-year Treasury yield remains anchored near 4.65-4.66%. Iran-Oman Hormuz talks remain unresolved and conditional (Iran continues to withhold full reopening pending U.S. concessions/compensation) -- progress-in-talks, not a resolved discontinuity, and no new kinetic escalation was identified this run. Alpha Vantage remained fully rate-limited on both the initial call and a retry (a ninth consecutive run), so this assessment again relies entirely on WebSearch; this run's NQ futures print via WebSearch was internally inconsistent (mismatched last-price vs bid/ask levels) and both investing.com and Yahoo Finance were blocked by the egress proxy when attempting to fetch a cleaner quote directly -- a genuine and further-degraded live intraday price-path limitation versus prior runs' merely-stale-but-consistent snapshot. Confidence is lowered accordingly this run.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Continue monitoring through the late European morning and into the 12:30 UTC Retail Sales and 14:00 UTC preliminary UMich sentiment cluster; an upgrade to a higher Tail state still requires observed persistent one-way structure with failed pullbacks in the broad Nasdaq-100 complex itself, not the pending data cluster, the unresolved Hormuz talks, the premarket chip rally, or this run's continued Alpha Vantage outage and internally inconsistent futures print.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures print could not be reliably pinned down this run (WebSearch returned an internally inconsistent quote; investing.com and Yahoo Finance both blocked); VIX flat near 14.4-14.8; 10Y anchored ~4.65-4.66%; chip stocks broadly firmer in premarket (Nvidia, TSMC, Broadcom, SK Hynix, Micron, AMD); Iran-Oman Hormuz talks remain unresolved/conditional with no new kinetic escalation; today's 12:30 UTC Retail Sales and 14:00 UTC preliminary UMich sentiment remain the session's main checkpoints; Alpha Vantage remains fully rate-limited for a ninth consecutive run, so Confidence eases further into the low band.
body: About 30-35 minutes past the top of the hour, conditions remain calm into the European late morning, roughly one hour on from the prior run. Thursday's session closed with the S&P 500 up 0.65% to a fresh record 7,798.99 (intraday high 7,816.70) and the Nasdaq Composite up 0.81% to 26,803.03, on soft July PPI reinforcing rate-cut expectations. This run's WebSearch results for Nasdaq 100 futures returned internally inconsistent figures (a last price around 29,853.25 alongside a bid/ask of 30,206.50/30,220.00 that do not reconcile), and direct attempts to fetch a cleaner live quote from investing.com and Yahoo Finance were both blocked by the egress proxy -- a genuine live intraday price-path limitation, distinct from and somewhat worse than prior runs' consistently-stale-but-at-least-coherent snapshot. VIX opened near 14.68 with today's range so far 14.39-14.80, essentially flat versus the prior run. The 10-year Treasury yield continues to hold near its recent range (~4.65-4.66%, last reliably observed Thursday); Alpha Vantage TREASURY_YIELD was retried once and both attempts returned an immediate rate_limit error, so yields again come from WebSearch context rather than a fresh pull. On the Strait of Hormuz, Iran continues to withhold a full reopening pending U.S. concessions and compensation even as Oman-brokered talks remain described as very close on managing the waterway -- this remains progress-in-talks rather than a resolved discontinuity, and no new kinetic escalation was identified this run. Semiconductors firmed broadly in premarket trading: Nvidia +1.82%, with TSMC, Broadcom, SK Hynix, Micron and AMD all up between roughly 2.7% and 4.3%, extending the prior run's overnight strength with no negative index-level semiconductor catalyst identified; Nvidia's August 26 earnings remain the next dedicated catalyst. Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily quota remains exhausted for a ninth consecutive run, so per the fallback protocol this assessment again relies entirely on WebSearch for yields, oil, VIX, equities and price-path context; combined with this run's internally inconsistent futures print and blocked direct-fetch attempts, evidence quality has degraded further, and Confidence eases to 34 (low, down from 37) to reflect that. Tail holds at 9% (still low; no persistent one-way structure evidence, and calm overnight/morning conditions plus a broad-based premarket chip rally are not themselves a Nasdaq-100 price-path signal) while Stress firms slightly to 27% (moderate, up from 25%) on generic pre-event positioning, with the main forecast driver remaining the pending 12:30 UTC Retail Sales / 14:00 UTC UMich cluster, which is projected to push Stress toward the upper-40s around the release before easing back through the afternoon, evening, and into the quiet Saturday handover.

lookbackSummary: Tail held in the low band (9-18%) through the full prior 24 hours as the index ground to a fresh S&P 500 record above 7,800 on soft PPI; Stress ran elevated to high (up to 58%) around the Wednesday/Thursday CPI-PPI and AMAT-earnings window before easing back into the low-to-moderate band (23-29%) through Friday's European morning as the after-hours reaction stayed contained to single names and no broader transmission was confirmed.
outlookSummary: Tail is projected to stay low (5-11%) through the next 24 hours; Stress is projected to build from the high-20s toward the upper-40s across the 12:30-14:00 UTC Retail Sales / UMich sentiment cluster and the U.S. cash-open/power-hour window before easing back through the evening and into the quiet Saturday handover, with no forecast slot currently implying an action change from EA_ON. Confidence is projected to stay in the low-to-medium-low band throughout, reflecting the continued Alpha Vantage outage and this run's inconsistent live futures print.

forecastDetail.comment: European mid/late morning: chip stocks broadly rallying in premarket (Nvidia, TSMC, Broadcom, SK Hynix, Micron, AMD all higher) after Thursday's soft-PPI record close; VIX flat near 14.4-14.8 and the 10Y holds ~4.65-4.66%. Alpha Vantage remained rate-limited on retry (ninth consecutive run) and this run's NQ futures print via WebSearch was internally inconsistent (mismatched last/bid-ask levels) with investing.com and Yahoo Finance both blocked by the egress proxy, a genuine and further-degraded live intraday price-path limitation.
Late European morning holds calm into the U.S. data cluster; Stress ticks up modestly on generic pre-event positioning ahead of Retail Sales.

Final hour before the 12:30 UTC Retail Sales print; Stress continues to build on forecast dispersion and event positioning while Tail stays anchored in the low band absent any observed persistent one-way structure in the Nasdaq-100 complex itself.

U.S. Retail Sales (July, 8:30am ET) prints within this hour -- consensus +0.3% MoM headline, +0.2% ex-auto -- the session's first major checkpoint; Stress rises toward the elevated band on event/whipsaw risk while Tail requires an observed failed-pullback/persistent-extension reaction before it could follow, which is not yet asserted.

University of Michigan preliminary consumer sentiment (August, 10am ET; consensus 54.1 vs 55.2 prior) prints within this hour on the heels of Retail Sales, keeping the window in event/whipsaw mode; Stress is projected to peak here before easing through the afternoon as the data cluster clears.
Data cluster has fully cleared; Stress begins easing back toward the moderate band into the U.S. cash-open/power-hour window, with Tail unchanged absent confirmed persistent one-way structure.
